title: FlexGNN: A High-Performance, Large-Scale Full-Graph GNN System with Best-Effort Training Plan Optimization

problem.claim: Full-graph GNN training must support complex application workloads while achieving high training speed and scale.

gap.claim: Existing full-graph training methods do not fully manage intermediate training data and rely on rigid inter-GPU communication, limiting training speed and scale.

contributions.claim: FlexGNN fully manages intermediate data and adaptively performs inter-GPU communication through generated and optimized best-effort training execution plans.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments are reported to show that FlexGNN outperforms existing full-graph GNN methods in training speed and scale.
FlexGNN is reported as up to 5.4X faster than HongTu and up to 95.5X faster than NeutronStar.

narrative_sequence.summary: Full-graph GNNs are increasingly used for complex problems such as weather forecasting and material discovery.
Existing training methods inadequately manage intermediate data and use rigid inter-GPU communication, constraining speed and scale.
FlexGNN addresses these limitations with full intermediate-data management, adaptive communication, and optimized best-effort execution plans.
The authors report substantial speed and scale advantages over existing methods, including HongTu and NeutronStar.

source_observation.claim: The proposed system jointly manages intermediate data and adapts inter-GPU communication through execution-plan optimization.

interpretation.claim: Training-system performance may benefit from coordinating data management, communication, and execution planning rather than optimizing them independently.

application.claim: For large-scale distributed graph workloads, consider adaptive execution planning that accounts for intermediate data and communication behavior.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond full-graph GNN training or across different hardware and workload conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, hardware configuration, graph sizes, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not define how training speed and scale are measured.
The abstract does not describe the execution-plan optimization algorithm or its overhead.
The abstract does not provide absolute runtime results or variance across experiments.
